subject.title: Reject unsupported diagnostics OTel grpc config

question: Should OpenClaw adopt this upgrade policy for shipped `diagnostics.otel.protocol: "grpc"` configs: doctor removes the unsupported value and disables only legacy configurations with active OTLP signals?
rationale: The code and focused proof establish a mechanically coherent migration, but only maintainers can choose whether the product should fail closed after repair, preserve the current no-export outcome by disabling telemetry, or retain another compatibility path.

options.title: Accept the doctor migration
options.body: Merge the narrow contract correction and value-aware doctor repair, keeping stdout-only logging enabled when no OTLP signal would run.

options.title: Choose a different upgrade policy
options.body: Keep the PR open while maintainers specify a different canonical migration outcome for existing enabled `grpc` configurations.

options.title: Retain grpc until exporter support exists
options.body: Reject the contract narrowing and leave the existing accepted-but-nonfunctional value in place pending real gRPC exporter support.

recommendation.title: Accept the doctor migration
recommendation.body: Merge the narrow contract correction and value-aware doctor repair, keeping stdout-only logging enabled when no OTLP signal would run.

likelyOwner.reason: The available timeline indicates direct involvement, while the remaining blocker is a product and upgrade-policy decision.
